name: Ollier Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Ollier Disease

criteria.description: Presence of multiple enchondromas predominantly in the metaphyseal regions of long bones
Asymmetric distribution of enchondromas leading to unilateral or asymmetric skeletal involvement
No family history of enchondromatosis, supporting nonhereditary nature
Radiographic evidence of bone deformities and cortical thinning associated with enchondromas
History or presence of pathologic fractures in affected bones

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple enchondromas with asymmetric distribution and characteristic radiographic bone deformities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not required; diagnosis primarily clinical and radiological.

pathognomonic.notes: Cartilage tumors within the medullary cavity of bones
Often unilateral or more severe on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone shortening and limb length discrepancy

common.notes: Localized pain related to enchondromas or fractures

occasional.notes: Due to joint involvement or deformity
From enchondromas impinging on adjacent nerves
searchTerms: tingling or weakness from nerve compression

occasional.notes: Secondary to deformity or nerve involvement

rare.notes: Occurs in a minority of cases, usually in adulthood
Delayed healing due to abnormal bone structure

imaging: Radiographs showing multiple enchondromas with characteristic metaphyseal location
MRI demonstrating cartilage lesions and extent of bone involvement
CT scan for detailed assessment of bone deformities and cortical thinning
genetic: Somatic mutations in IDH1 and IDH2 genes identified in enchondromas
other: Physical examination revealing asymmetric limb deformities and palpable bony masses

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple enchondromas plus soft tissue hemangiomas
Cutaneous vascular lesions absent in Ollier disease
Presence of multiple osteochondromas (bone outgrowths) rather than enchondromas
Lesions typically arise from bone surface

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of bony lesions
New onset of severe localized bone pain
Signs of malignant transformation such as soft tissue mass or pathological fracture
references: Wheeler, D. L., et al. Ollier disease: clinical and radiographic features. Radiographics. 2019.
Amary, M. F., et al. IDH1 and IDH2 mutations are frequent in Ollier disease and Maffucci syndrome. Nat Genet. 2011.
